limitations: Two source-review references are fallible, not absolute gold; citation validation does not prove label correctness.
Blinding is instructional, not access-isolated. Same-model Grok proposer/judge: no independent-model claim.
Calibration and heldout are reported separately; no tuning, parameter search or heldout-based selection is performed.
Failed calls remain in every denominator and map to unverifiable in confusion/truth agreement; successfulTruthAgreement excludes them from matches only.
Failed calls have null nonObvious and count as disagreement, not an invented false label. Zero-denominator metrics are not estimable.
One pinned repository and this fixed claim mix do not establish general accuracy; absent classes cannot establish class performance.

prediction.reason: The test expects testTuple.parse(new Array(3)) to throw. The tuple has three items, so a length-3 sparse array still fails; length match alone does not make parsing succeed.
Tests expect issues.length 2 when addIssue omits fatal and parses 1234 as string, and length 1 when fatal:true; the extra issue is the downstream string type failure.
Lines 15-19 call .nonstrict().parse(...) with no expect().toThrow() and no assertion on the return value, so the test only fails if parse throws.
The test JSON.parses a "__proto__" key and only expects obj1.a undefined; it is not an object literal and never asserts the key is dropped rather than kept safely.
The require test only constructs baseSchema then discards it; the .require() call and all expect assertions are commented out, so it asserts nothing.
Test "safeparse unexpected error" expects a refine callback that throws to make safeParse throw (toThrow), not return success:false.
The test parses undefined without expecting a throw and asserts parse(null) and parse("") throw, so void rejects those nothing-like values rather than accepting them.
Lines 40-41 push datetimeBenchmarks.suites for --discriminatedUnion, not discriminatedUnionBenchmarks.suites, and the loop then runs those suites.
The test builds z.literal from a Symbol and parse()s that same instance in the passing suite; a new Symbol("terrific") is expected to throw.

Lines 8–23 only build mapped types and call util.assertEqual with those type args plus literal true; no expect/toEqual. The never check exists only in erased type positions, so it cannot run at test t
Expects show the refine message only in formErrors and path ["a"]/["b"] issues under fieldErrors, but never an empty path or a general routing rule for any non-empty path.
Only ipv4RegexB matches each octet alternative via (?=(...))\N lookahead plus backreference; A and C–I use ordinary grouped alternation for octets (G/H lookaheads are only (?!$)).
The named test safeParses {people:[123]} against z.string().array().min(2) and asserts error.issues.length === 2, so both the type and min-length failures are reported.
DeepPartial's chain matches only ZodObject, ZodArray, ZodOptional, ZodNullable, and ZodTuple, then ends in `: T`, so every other ZodTypeAny is returned unchanged.
Exclusive too_big dates say 'smaller than', not 'less than'; only numbers use 'less than'. Strings do use 'over'/'under', and wording is type-specific.
manySuite only adds valid: a and valid: c; the four-variant union includes bSchema and dSchema but never valid: b or valid: d.
The formatting test expects format() to leave non-failing array indices undefined (error.inner?.name?.[1], and [0]/[1]/[2] when only the array refine fails), not {_errors:[]} objects.
Scalars is defined as Primitive | Primitive[], so it is one primitive or one flat Primitive[] and excludes nested arrays.
Passing validations calls minCheck and maxCheck parse on the exact benchmark date with no toThrow, while dates outside that bound throw, so the test treats both bounds as inclusive.
min(5).min(10)→10 and max(5).max(1)→1 match both overwrite and the stricter bound, so the test does not show replacement rather than combining.
The first test expects schema.parse to throw for an async refine resolving false and for Promise.resolve(true), so sync parse is asserted to throw even when the check would pass.
CastToStringTuple's else branch is never and UnionToTupleString<T> is unconstrained, so a non-string union becomes never with no type error.
Tests delete Date, Set, or Map one at a time, then assert z.object({}).safeParse({}).success is true.
success 2 calls parse on a plain {then(),catch()} object with no throw, while a non-function catch throws, so the check is structural not instanceof Promise.
All ten cases whose names include "invalid" wrap parse in try/catch with an empty catch (e) {}, so the error is discarded and never inspected or asserted.
Line 77 asserts promise().readonly() infers Promise<string>, not Readonly<...>; lines 249-253 assert Object.isFrozen on the awaited parseAsync result, so the type hides the freeze.
Line 3 exports filePath from undeclared ambient __filename; the file also exports schema, inferred type, and instance fixtures (Test and variants).
hair and active both read i before str/num/array increment it; odd i is blue and true, even is brown and false, so they are locked together.
Reverse-then-overwrite makes contextual (listed first) the final message, matching the comment that it is first priority, not the opposite of that order.
The named test parses Map([[42, Symbol()]]) and asserts two invalid_type issues, at paths [0,"key"] and [0,"value"], not one combined issue.
The test expects issues.length 1 for both "12345" and "3". "12345" would also fail the piped v<100 refine if it ran, so one issue means later stages add none.
The base64 validations test lists "" in validBase64Strings with the comment that an empty string is technically valid base64, and the loop asserts safeParse(str).success is true.
The test passes abstract class AbstractBar to z.instanceof and calls AbstractSchema.parse(new Bar("asdf")) on the success path, unlike cases wrapped in toThrow.
The 'from const' test parses 3 (Gamma) with no throw and expects parse(2) to throw, so only actual member values pass, not any number.
The string params test uses (x) => typeof x !== "number" then safeParse(1234), asserting failure whose error includes "customerr"—the inverse of the number check.
manySuite valid cases only call many.parse(objA) and many.parse(objC); the [a,b,c,d] union never valid-parses b or d (no objD, objB only used on doubleSuite).
The named test asserts set issue paths [0] and [1], but this file never shows map key/value paths, so the contrast is not settled.
Capture-groups uses the full Gregorian test, but the leap-year regex also encodes the 400-year century exception, not a divisible-by-4-only approximation.
The test only passes plain status-bearing object literals to the predicates; it never shows their implementations, so pure structural checks versus identity or prototype checks are not settled.
Test only asserts safeParse(1234) fails with issues[0] invalid_type; it does not check that this is the sole issue, that toUpperCase was skipped, or that no TypeError escaped.
stringSchema.parse is called with empty, short, and long; optional and nullable cases call parse only with long (nullable also parses null).
Only uncommented test is the empty test("", () => {}) on line 11; the describe and all Go-To-Definition cases plus the helper are // commented and do not run.
Test only shows the intersection fails with invalid_intersection_types after a transform appends an element; it never parses each branch alone or mentions a deep-equality merge.
age assertions set z.input equal to plain number, z.infer equal to number & BRAND<"age">, and those two unequal, so the brand stays off the input type.
The complex-chain test chains catch("qwer").removeCatch() after an earlier catch("asdf") and asserts parse(15) and parse(true) equal "ASDF!", not an error or "asdfasdf".
getValidEnumValues keeps keys only when typeof obj[obj[k]] !== "number", which drops TS numeric-enum reverse keys that map back to numbers.
Cycle handlers do use (emptySuite|shortSuite|longSuite as any).name and constructors take name strings, but Benchmark.Suite's type is not cited so the missing typed name is unshown.
The test only expects parse(undefined) to equal "outer" and never inspects schema shape, so it does not show the inner default was discarded rather than wrapped and unused.
"catchall overrides strict" parses unknown numeric keys after .strict().catchall(z.number()) without throwing; comments say catchall overrides unknownKeys and validates those keys.
flatten() keys fieldErrors only by sub.path[0] (lines 307-309) and drops deeper segments; format() walks the full path into a nested _errors tree (lines 238-260). Signatures do not state that split.
Live tests use z.late.object and z.lazy for the same Category type and each calls parse on the shared testCategory without expecting failure.
The test sets description via z.string({ description }) and expects it after both .optional() and .optional().nullable().default("default"), a three-wrapper chain.
expect is imported but never called; the test only reads Mocker properties as bare statements, so it passes if access does not throw and asserts no values.
checkErrors is called on z.tuple([]) and z.unknown() plus string/number/boolean/undefined/null; if optional().parse(bad) throws, it expects formErrors to equal the unwrapped parse's formErrors.
The test re-augments species from z.string() to z.array(z.string()); an array parses and a string throws, so the existing key schema is replaced, not merged.
@ts-expect-error marks explicit false in pick/omit masks; parse tests then succeed and fail as if that key were absent (name-only pick, name-only omit).
chained mixed refining types types superRefine as `arg is secondRefinement` and assertEqual checks the next refine callback's arg, not only final z.infer.
The 'nested no undefined' test uses z.string().or(z.array(z.string())) without .optional(), asserts type {inner: string|string[]}, and safeParse of undefined fails.
Uncalled `.toBeNull;` appears only in "min max getters" (lines 103–128). "int getter" has no `.toBeNull`; it only uses invoked `.toEqual(...)`.
Lines 10–186 are comments with 25 pick/omit/mask tests; the only live case is test("test", () => { z; }) with no expect or parse.
Test "promise async parse bad" expects safeParseAsync(Promise.resolve("XXX")) success:true, then data rejects with ZodError.
errToObj uses message||{} so undefined becomes {}; toString uses message?.message, which yields undefined, not "".
Bigint throws are commented not ZodError and number throws as ZodError, but string and boolean have no failures, and date BigInt is marked not a ZodError.
Cited lines 1-30 only show "type guard" and "test this binding"; no dateSchema, parseAsync, try/catch, or invalid_date assertion appears, so the claim is unsettled.
symbol returns the module-level testSymbol, while string/number/bigint/boolean/date each call Math.random() on access, so repeated .symbol reads are the same reference.
The parse test calls crazySchema.parse(...) and discards the result; expect is imported but unused, so failure only happens if parse throws.
The int test asserts with expect(() => int.parse(3.5)).toThrow() outside any try/catch, so a non-throw fails the test; instantiation also has no parseAsync try/catch.
The enum and nativeEnum test uses z.enum(["b","c"]) and z.nativeEnum(MyEnum) as branch discriminators and parse()s b, c, MyEnum.d, MyEnum.e, and "e", which would throw if rejected.
Test 'return dirty result over aborted' expects that one custom issue only as the dirty refine branch's own error, not a synthesized issue whenever every union option fails.
The file has no test named "test this binding" and never calls safeParse; callbacks invoke parse/parseAsync on existing schemas, not a new z.string().safeParse.
The test uses .args(z.string()).implement((str,_arg,_qewr)=>...) as Array.filter and expects length 2, so extra call args are accepted and unused.

trim, toLowerCase, and toUpperCase each inline new ZodString({...this._def, checks:[...this._def.checks,{kind}]}) matching _addCheck; email, url, min, max, regex and the other check methods call this.
exclude(foods) is asserted equal to z.ZodEnum<[]> only under @ts-expect-error TS2344, while z.infer<typeof EmptyFoodEnum> is asserted equal to never with no error.
overrideErrorMap is one module-level let; setErrorMap overwrites it and getErrorMap always returns it, with no schema or parse-call argument to scope the change.
Line 28 builds the field with z.object({ points: z.number() }).nonstrict(), an active call, not .passthrough() or .strict().
The test expects safeParse({ array: [] }).success toBe(false), not true. A comment notes the bug; the assertion does not claim success.
